title: AGST 50104 Syllabus
text:
AGST 50104


The course develops the ability to choose experimental designs, formulate fixed- and random-effect models, conduct ANOVA and mixed-model analyses, evaluate assumptions, and communicate results in agricultural and biological research.


By the end of the course, students should be able to:

Apply replication, randomization, and blocking to plan valid experiments.
Select an appropriate CRD, RCBD, factorial, split-plot, or incomplete-block design.
Translate research hypotheses into models with correctly specified fixed and random effects.
Conduct ANOVA, linear mixed-model, and generalized linear-model analyses with appropriate diagnostics.
Distinguish statistical significance from practical importance and communicate the results.
Recognize pseudoreplication, confounding, and incorrect error terms.

title: Group Project: Incomplete Block Designs
text:
AGST 50104 · GROUP PROJECT


This project was completed by a team of four students. It brought together experimental-design theory, a practical agricultural or biological application, statistical analysis, model diagnostics, interpretation, and scientific communication.


TEAM4 collaborators

Shared research, analysis, slide development, and presentation responsibilities.



FORMATRecorded presentation

The team presented the completed slide deck while recording the presentation.



DELIVERYYouTube submission

The recording was published on YouTube and its link was shared with the professor for grading.





The work examined incomplete block designs, including balanced incomplete block designs (BIBD) and alpha designs. These designs are useful when a complete block cannot accommodate every treatment and the experiment must retain useful treatment comparisons under practical constraints.

Topic understanding and explanation

title: CHEM 58103 Lectures
text:
LECTURE INDEX · EXAM I FOUNDATION

Chapters 1–6
The supplied slide decks contain 452 slides across six chapters. This index records their conceptual scope without redistributing copyrighted slide content. The Fall 2026 syllabus assigns Chapters 2–6 to Exam I; Chapter 1 remains a course foundation.


CH 01 · 58 SLIDES ### Biochemistry and the unity of life Chemical foundations, cellular organization, evolution, energy, and the molecular logic of living systems.


CH 02 · 105 SLIDES ### Protein composition and architecture Amino acids, peptide bonds, secondary structure, folding, domains, quaternary structure, and protein modification.


CH 03 · 92 SLIDES ### Exploring proteins and proteomes Purification, chromatography, electrophoresis, antibodies, mass spectrometry, sequencing, X-ray crystallography, and NMR.


CH 04 · 81 SLIDES ### DNA, RNA, and the flow of information Nucleic-acid structure, replication, transcription, RNA processing, translation, and the genetic code.


CH 05 · 71 SLIDES ### Genes and genomes Restriction enzymes, sequencing, PCR, cloning, expression analysis, genome editing, transgenic models, and gene therapy.


CH 06 · 45 SLIDES ### Evolution and bioinformatics Homology, sequence alignment, substitution matrices, BLAST, structural conservation, phylogeny, and horizontal gene transfer.

Chapter descriptions were independently summarized from the supplied lecture decks. The decks identify Biochemistry, 8th edition (Macmillan Education, 2015) and John Tymoczko in their metadata.
